title: Other Major Global Economic & Trade Bodies
shortDescription: OECD, OPEC, UNCTAD, BIS, and the regional development banks that keep showing up in exam questions.
genZNote: The economic organizations that don't fit neatly into 'UN agency' or 'Bretton Woods twin' — but still get asked about constantly.

sections.heading: OECD — Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
bullets: Established 1961 (successor to the OEEC, which coordinated Marshall Plan aid after WWII); headquartered in Paris.
A group of mostly high-income, market-economy countries that coordinate economic policy and publish widely-used comparative data/reports (e.g. PISA education rankings).
India is NOT a member of the OECD, though it engages as a 'Key Partner' country.

sections.heading: OPEC and OPEC+
bullets: OPEC — Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries — established 1960 at the Baghdad Conference; headquartered in Vienna, Austria.
Coordinates petroleum policy among major oil-exporting members to stabilize oil markets and secure member revenues.

OPEC+ is a broader, informal coalition of OPEC members plus other major oil-exporting non-members (e.g. Russia) that coordinates production levels jointly — OPEC+ is NOT a formal treaty organization the way OPEC itself is.

sections.heading: UNCTAD — UN Conference on Trade and Development
sections.body: Established 1964 as a UN General Assembly body (a programme, not a specialized agency), headquartered in Geneva. UNCTAD focuses on integrating developing countries into the world economy, particularly on trade, investment, and development finance issues — it is the UN's own trade-and-development voice, distinct from the WTO, which is an independent treaty organization outside the UN system.

rows: Harmonizes customs procedures and classification (the HS commodity code system) worldwide.
'Central bank for central banks' — fosters cooperation among national central banks and monetary authorities.
Monitors and makes recommendations on the global financial system, set up after the 2008 financial crisis.
Regional development bank for Asia-Pacific; India is a founding member (1966).
China-initiated multilateral development bank focused on infrastructure; India is the largest borrower and second-largest shareholder after China.
Founded by the BRICS grouping (2014/2015) to fund infrastructure and sustainable development in emerging economies.

sections.heading: The Exam Angle on These Bodies
bullets: Headquarters city is the single most commonly tested fact for this whole group — learn the table above by HQ city first.

India's membership status varies sharply across this list: OECD (not a member, Key Partner), ADB (founding member), AIIB (major shareholder/borrower), NDB (founding member) — do not assume uniform membership across 'similar-sounding' bodies.

UNCTAD vs WTO is a classic confusion pair: UNCTAD is a UN body advocating for developing countries' trade interests; WTO is an independent treaty organization that actually administers binding trade rules.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Beyond IMF/World Bank/WTO, global economic governance also runs through bodies like OECD, OPEC, UNCTAD, BIS, and the regional development banks (ADB, AIIB, NDB).
keyFacts: OECD (1961, Paris) — India is a Key Partner, not a member.
OPEC (1960, Vienna) vs OPEC+ (informal, broader coalition including Russia).
UNCTAD (1964, Geneva) — a UN body, distinct from the independent WTO.
ADB (Manila) — India founding member; AIIB (Beijing) — India major shareholder/borrower; NDB (Shanghai) — BRICS-founded.
commonConfusion: OPEC (a formal organization) and OPEC+ (an informal wider coalition) are not the same thing — Russia is in OPEC+ but not OPEC.
India's membership varies across ADB/AIIB/NDB/OECD — never assume the same status applies to all 'similar' bodies.

highYieldFacts: OECD HQ: Paris. OPEC HQ: Vienna. UNCTAD HQ: Geneva. BIS HQ: Basel. ADB HQ: Manila. AIIB HQ: Beijing. NDB HQ: Shanghai.
India is NOT an OECD member but IS a founding member of ADB and NDB, and a major shareholder in AIIB.
UNCTAD is a UN programme; WTO is an independent treaty organization — they are not the same kind of body.
commonTraps: Don't assume OPEC+ has the same membership as OPEC — OPEC+ includes non-OPEC oil exporters like Russia.
Don't confuse BIS (central-bank cooperation) with IMF (member-state monetary support) — different mandates.
mustRemember: AIIB: China largest shareholder, India second-largest.
NDB: founded by BRICS (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa).
possibleQuestions: Where is the headquarters of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank?
Is India a member of the OECD?
